requirement:
TypeScript and TSX report only `Comment` attachments. Both recognize `//`
line comments and `/* … */` block comments, including `/** … */`
documentation comments. Decorators remain part of the parsed source.
rationale:
The reviewed test adequately checks `requirements.sdk.sources.typescript.attachments`. I did not read the implementation, because the supplied test input was enough to judge adequacy. The test is `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[bundled_languages_classify_only_their_attachment_syntax]`. It carries a `{test}` reference to the subject. Obligations and the scenarios that cover them: - **Only `Comment` attachments are reported.** For `test.ts` and `test.tsx`, the test sorts all attachments found on outline items and asserts exact equality with the expected `(kind, text)` list. Every entry is `Comment`, and the list is exact. An `Annotation` or any other extra attachment for `@dec class C {}` would therefore fail the assertion. - **`//` line comments are recognized.** `// trailing` is expected in both the `test.ts` and `test.tsx` cases. - **`/* … */` block comments, including `/** … */`, are recognized.** `test.ts` expects `/** doc */`. `test.tsx` expects `/* doc */`. Together they cover the documentation form and the ordinary block form, and each is run in the language where the requirement says both are recognized. The TS case has no plain `/* */` comment. The TSX case supplies one, and `/** */` is itself a block comment, so I do not count this as a gap. - **Comment-like text that is not a comment is not reported.** `'// string'` in `test.ts` and the JSX text `

// text

` in `test.tsx` are excluded by the exact-list assertion. This guards against a naive text scan. - **Decorators remain part of the parsed source.** For `test.ts` and `test.tsx`, the test asserts that `snapshot.text()` contains `@dec class C`. It also asserts that no decorator attachment is reported. No relevant obligation is untested, and the assertions enforce the expected outcomes.
